definition: Ossify means to become rigid and stop changing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ossify. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ossify should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The chef worried that the menu had begun to ossify: the 'seasonal specials' had not changed in four years.
Habits can harden and still be broken with effort; hardening is the milder, earlier stage of what ossify completes.
Fossilize goes further than ossify: the ossified rulebook still runs the club, while the fossilized one survives only as a curiosity from another age.

Calcify means to stiffen with mineral deposits, and figuratively to grow inflexible. It is ossify's near-twin — one image from lime, one from bone — and like ossify it describes something still standing and still in force, just no longer able to bend.

Stagnate means to stop moving or developing, like still water going stale. A stagnant committee produces nothing new but could still change course; to ossify is to harden past the point where change is possible. Stagnation is idleness; ossifying is rigidity.
to change to fit new conditions
to keep developing over time

Latin os, 'bone,' survives in English almost nowhere outside the anatomy lab — ossuary, a chamber for storing bones, is its rare other descendant — so there is no everyday relative to lean on. The familiar half is the suffix: -ify, 'to make,' the same maker that builds mollify, vilify, and stupefy in this unit.
Ossify means to become rigid and stop changing.
Grandpa's morning route had ossified decades ago — the same bench, the same crossword, the same two slices of rye — and the family learned that even a new toaster counted as an upheaval.
Ossify is literally 'to turn to bone,' and the figurative sense keeps that image: habits, institutions, or opinions that were once living and flexible harden until they cannot bend without breaking.
Ossify is the pointed choice for institutions, rules, and thinking that have stopped being able to change — it diagnoses, where 'harden' merely describes.
Its unit-mate mollify makes a neat opposite pair to remember: one word softens, the other turns to bone.

The academy's fencing curriculum was once the envy of Europe, revised yearly as masters returned from tournaments with new footwork.
Somewhere in the last century the revisions stopped, and the syllabus began to ossify.
The forms are still taught in strict order, the examinations still enforced to the letter; nothing has been abandoned, and nothing can be touched.
When a young instructor proposed adding a single modern parry, the committee did not reject the idea so much as fail to locate any procedure by which an idea could be considered.
Visitors sometimes mistake the stillness for decline, but the school is thriving by every measure it recognizes — enrollment is full, the drills immaculate, the year 1911 preserved in amber.
